claims.text: Pain < 4 to 6 wks: USU ⍉testing, unless there are red flags, a serious inj, or signs of a specific nonmechanical cause (eg, pyelonephritis).
claims.quote: Usually, if duration of pain is short (< 4 to 6 weeks), no testing is required unless red flag findings are present, patients have had a serious injury (eg, vehicular crash, fall from a height, penetrating trauma), or evaluation suggests a specific nonmechanical cause (eg, pyelonephritis).

claims.text: Neuro deficits suggesting n. root or spinal cord compress: MRI (less often CT myelography) ASAP.
claims.quote: Neurologic deficits, particularly those consistent with nerve root compression or spinal cord compression: MRI and less commonly CT myelography, done as soon as possible

claims.text: Poss infect: WBC count, ESR and/or CRP, imaging (USU MRI or CT) and cx of infected tissue.
claims.quote: Possible infection: White blood cell (WBC) count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and/or C-reactive protein (CRP), imaging (usually MRI or CT), and culture of infected tissue

claims.text: Poss CA: CT or MRI, CBC, and possibly bx.
claims.quote: Possible cancer: CT or MRI, complete blood count (CBC), and possibly biopsy

claims.text: Poss aneurysm: CT, angio or sometimes US; poss aortic dissection: angio, CT or MRI.
claims.quote: Possible aneurysm: CT, angiography, or sometimes ultrasound Possibleaortic dissection: Angiography, CT, or MRI

claims.text: Disabling or persistent > 6 wks: imaging (USU MRI or CT), plus WBC, ESR and/or CRP if infect = sus.
claims.quote: Symptoms that are disabling or persistent > 6 weeks: Imaging (usually MRI or CT) and, if infection is suspected, WBC count, ESR, and/or CRP

claims.text: Extraspinal Eti: eg, CXR for pulm disorders, UA for urinary tract disorders or back pain w ⍉clear mech cause.
claims.quote: Other extraspinal disorders: Testing as appropriate (eg, chest radiograph for pulmonary disorders, urinalysis for urinary tract disorders or for back pain with no clear mechanical cause)
